prompt:
A high-speed motorboat travels across a lake at a constant speed of 14 m s^-1.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Motorboat moving horizontally at speed v = 14 m s^-1. Propeller thrust T acts forward. Hydrodynamic drag force D = c v^2 opposes the motion, with c = 28 N s^2 m^-2.]
The water resistance D opposing the boat is given by D = c v^2, where c = 28 N s^2 m^-2 and v is the speed in m s^-1.
(a) Calculate the drag force on the boat when v = 14 m s^-1. [1]
(b) Calculate the useful power output delivered by the engine at this speed. [1]
(c) The boat engine has a maximum useful power output of 115 kW. Calculate the maximum theoretical speed of the boat on the lake. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Calculates drag force: D = 28 * 14^2 = 5490 N (accept 5500 N or 5488 N).
(b) Calculates power: P = Dv = 5488 * 14 = 76 800 W (accept 77 kW or 76.8 kW).
(c) Sets up cubic equation: P = c v^3 => v^3 = 115 000 / 28 = 4107.
(c) Calculates maximum speed: v = (4107)^(1/3) = 16.0 m s^-1 (accept 16 m s^-1).

hints: In (a), use D = c v^2 with c = 28 and v = 14.
In (c), solve P = c v^3 for v by taking the cube root of P / c.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (b): P = Fv = 5488 * 14 = 76 832 W approx 77 kW.
